articles.titleOriginal: Nuri rocket successfully completes 5th flight
articles.titleJa: Nuriロケットが5回目の飛行を成功裏に完了
articles.summaryJa: 韓国で自国開発されたNuriロケットは、水曜日、全南光州特別首都圏のGoheungにあるNaro Space Centerからの5回目の打ち上げを成功裏に完了し、15個の衛星のうち14個を軌道に投入した。
articles.summaryOriginal: Korea’s home-developed Nuri rocket successfully completed its fifth launch from the Naro Space Center in Goheung, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City, Wednesday, deploying 14 of 15 satellites into orbit. The rocket released five NEONSAT microsatellites and nine CubeSats at an altitude of 570 kilometers during its roughly 20-minute flight. The mission demonstrated Korea’s expanded ability to deploy multiple satellites and supported the development of privately led commercial launch services. The Nuri rocket lifts off at the launchpad of the Naro Space Center in Goheung, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City, Wednesday. Courtesy of Korea Aerospace Research Institute

articles.titleOriginal: Private sector's role increased in 5th Nuri launch
articles.titleJa: 5回目のNuriローンチで民間セクターの役割が強化されました
articles.summaryJa: Nuriは、水曜日の午後12時25分にGoheungのNaro Space Centerで5回目の打ち上げを完了し、Hanwha Aerospaceははるかに大きな運用上の役割を果たしました。
articles.summaryOriginal: Nuri completed its fifth launch at the Naro Space Center in Goheung at 12:25 p.m. Wednesday, with Hanwha Aerospace taking a much larger operational role. Hanwha deployed 42 staffers and directly operated controls at 18 of 22 launch-control consoles. KARI retained overall command, but responsibilities will shift further to Hanwha from the sixth launch in 2027 and are expected to transfer fully by the eighth launch. The Nuri rocket lifts off at the launchpad of the Naro Space Center in Goheung, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City, Wednesday. Korea Times photo by Shim Hyun-chul
